sources.title: GTA 6 Fan Says Rockstar Sent Them a Poster Just Because They Asked Nicely
sources.text: A Grand Theft Auto 6 fan in Brazil said they politely asked the Rockstar Games team to send them a poster – and it looks like they actually followed through. Reddit user aogustoo shared their story in a post late last month. What began as a "shot-in-the-dark email" they sent to Rockstar asking for a signed GTA 6 poster has turned into what seems to be a heartwarming moment for them and the community. "A while ago I took a complete shot in the dark and emailed Rockstar," they said. "I shared how hyped I was for GTA VI and asked if there was any chance I could get a poster for my room. "Honestly, I expected an automated reply or nothing at all. To my absolute surprise, an executive actually answered and shipped an official GTA VI poster straight from their New York office to my home in Brazil." You can see images, which show not only the poster but the emails they supposedly sent to receive it, above. As Rockstar (and the rest of the world) count down the days to GTA 6's November 19 launch, fans will no doubt be on the lookout for official merchandise like this. As many have pointed out, it's unclear if Rockstar truly took the time to send the poster, but the community is still looking to the moment as something worth celebrating as the countdown continues. "This is a massive W tho," Rockstar content creator @videotech said on X/Twitter . "This guy isn’t an influencer or someone famous, literally just a random Rockstar fan. Very kind of Rockstar and Take-Two to take the time and effort to do this." "​I blurred out all personal addresses, names, and contact emails to respect their privacy," aogustoo added. "Please don't flood their inbox with requests, as I'm pretty sure this was just a rare act of kindness from someone on their team." There's still so much about GTA 6 that we don’t know, but one thing is for sure: Rockstar will probably get even more emails after this. While we wait to learn more about the next Grand Theft Auto game ahead of its November 19 launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, you can check out IGN's recent interview with Rockstar North's Rob Nelson . You can also read about what Nintendo had to say about the chances of seeing GTA 6 on Switch 2 , some recently revealed radio stations , and even a batch of new screenshots . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. sources.name: Xbox Wire
sources.title: DMZ — 5 Features to Get Excited for in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s New Mode
sources.text: Call of Duty’s upcoming DMZ mode sounds like it’s shaping up to be something special. Set on the new Hajin map and inspired by the events and locations from Modern Warfare 4 ’s Campaign, this open-world combat environment will challenge you to loot, complete objectives, fight both enemies and rival Operators, and extract before everything you’ve earned is lost. Recent intel drops on the official Call of Duty Blog have given us a much clearer picture of what awaits in Hajin when DMZ launches as part of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . Players who have digitally pre-ordered or pre-purchased Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 can gain Early Access to the game’s Campaign starting Friday, October 16 and all of DMZ starting Tuesday, October 20. The events within DMZ are set after the main MW4 Campaign, leaving a power vacuum in its wake. Now it’s up to you to identify a new, mysterious threat and dismantle its operations across the DMZ through various deployments. From scavenging for crafting materials and experimenting with new technology, to leveling up an Operator, the mode sounds like it offers plenty to look forward to. Here are five features to get excited for when you begin your deployment. The 3D Printer will be available back at the Forward Operating Base (FOB) between deployments and will serve as your primary crafting station to build equipment and upgrades for your loadout before you drop into Hajin. The Call of Duty Blog shares that , as you progress through the DMZ, you’ll unlock new crafting recipes to create more powerful equipment – as well as upgrades to the 3D Printer and even the Forward Operating Base itself. Recipes can also be found on deployments and, presuming you extract in one piece, you can then craft those items for your Operator back at the FOB. When focused on crafting new equipment, the two key things you’ll be looking for when looting on deployments will be Resources and 3D Printer Ingredients – these are the two types of main elements to craft all items. There are four basic Resources to find during a deployment: Synthetics, Electronics, Chemicals, and Metals, automatically broken down from looted items, into your Backpack and Stash. 3D Printer Ingredients are rarer materials found in specific areas of Hajin and are valuable as an ingredient to make a new Item. Examples include Binding Catalyst, Biomaterials, Detonators, and Control Units, to name a few. Once you have enough of these two types of materials, you can select how many copies of an item you want to craft at once, then choose where crafted items go: send completed items directly to your Stash for later or equip them directly to your Operator to quickly prepare for the next deployment. Having this flexibility in how you want to engage the enemy during your deployment can open a variety of experiences in DMZ and can make each deployment feel like it matters, even if you come back to the FOB with zero kills to your name – at least you’ve got handful of electronics or a comms module to make it worth your time. Extraction shooters are always more engaging when every deployment has a clear purpose. That’s not going to be problem with DMZ as it will offer three ways to deploy: Story Missions, Dynamic Operations, and Free Roam. Of those, Story Missions and Dynamic Operations are two that really stand out with their defined objectives and high-tier rewards. According to the Call of Duty Blog , Story Missions will feature narrative-led deployments that you can complete and replay, though some remain locked until prerequisites are met. Each entry provides briefing intel, required objectives, and rewards – usually high-value gear and DMZ Cash – along with options for a random mission and additional milestone rewards. Dynamic Operations, meanwhile, give squads multiple goals to pursue within the DMZ. After deploying, you choose an operation and complete its objectives to earn DMZ XP, Cash, and the ability to call in a Supply Drop filled with unpredictable loot. That extra payoff adds anticipation to every successful Op while making Dynamic Operations a promising source of both Cash and XP. Persistent Operators may be DMZ’s most exciting feature because they allow Hajin to leave a lasting mark on you. You’ll begin with two Operator slots, and unlock a third as you progress through DMZ levels. Each Operator then grows stronger by surviving deployments and earning DMZ XP. Each successful exfil levels up your Operator’s Dog Tags, and this is the key to gaining Trait Points for your Operator. You can invest those points across the Warfighter, Scout, and Survivalist Trait Trees, creating a meaningful choice between specialization and flexibility: with a maximum of 18 points to earn, and a choice of over 60 Trait Points to augment your Operator, you can tailor each Operator to your skills and preferred role. For example, Warfighter Traits include Combat Resistance, Quick Fix, and Viper Sense; Scout Traits include improved Thermal Padding, UAV Upgrade, and Field Crafting; while Survivalist Traits include Faster and Free Revives, increased Consumable Duration, and many more. But here’s where it gets dicey: if an Operator fails to extract and becomes MIA, you must either recover them with DMZ Cash or dismiss them. Because recovery costs rise with Trait investment, bringing back a high-level Operator becomes increasingly expensive. Recovered Operators keep their Traits but lose their gear, putting real weight behind every deployment. The chase for loot is at the heart of every extraction shooter, and DMZ makes each haul matter beyond the current deployment. Returning to base with a pack full of supplies doesn’t just feel rewarding – it improves your chances of success the next time you enter Hajin. Once you drop into a deployment, looting should be a top priority. Searching containers provides resources for combat, supports marked Operations, strengthens your position in Hajin, and offers a reliable way to earn DMZ XP and adva

sources.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Launch Rollout Adds DMZ Early Access
sources.text: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month. Activision and Infinity Ward revealed a host of new details for its DMZ revamp in a blog post shared today. Early access for the mode joins campaign early access , with both available to those who pre-ordered either the standard or Vault Edition versions of the game across PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and/or Xbox Series X/S. Here's the full breakdown: Eligible players will gain early access to the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign starting Friday, October 16. DMZ early access will then follow Tuesday, October 20, with the full launch unleashing the rest of the experience come Friday, October 23. All of the new details arrived with a new gameplay trailer for DMZ, which you can see below. DMZ was first introduced as Call of Duty's take on the extraction shooter experience with 2022's Modern Warfare 2 . It was expanded upon in the months that followed but was ultimately deemed to be an underwhelming prototype by many. Support ended in late 2023, and now, Activision is taking another swing at it. The DMZ in Modern Warfare 4 has been propped up as a fully fleshed-out evolution for the game mode. In today's post, Infinity Ward described the new take on the mode as the series' "definitive extraction shooter experience," promising persistent progression in the open-world combat environment known as the Hajin Exclusion Zone. "There's an interesting story with the DMZ beta, where we had to make some decisions," studio multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot said in a recent behind-the-scenes video (below). "Certain things we wanted to do, we couldn't do. At the end of the day, we learned a lot: That we made a very approachable, fun sandbox that was fun to fight in, to explore, to make friends in, to get into fights in. There's a bunch of stuff we left on the table, so as soon as we finished with the last game, we were just gung-ho on, 'OK, we know what we want to do.'" Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 for PC and consoles. Our first proper look at DMZ gameplay arrived in June, with even more details shared earlier this week. While early access players will get to dive into DMZ and the story mode a few days earlier than others, core multiplayer offerings won't officially launch until that firm release date hits. You can see how the team at Infinity Ward is working to deal with wall-hack cheaters here . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. sources.title: Shadow of the Road delayed to March 10, 2027
sources.text: Publisher Owlcat Games and developer Another Angle Games have delayed story-driven turn-based RPG Shadow of the Road from its previously planned November 12, 2026 release date to March 10, 2027. It will be available for PC via Steam , Epic Games Store , and GOG . Here is the full explanation from Owlcat Games: This extra time will let the developers address remaining issues and give the whole experience the polish it deserves. The team will refine the tactical aspect of the encounters and fine-tune combat balance. It is of great importance that the positioning, initiative and ability choices all play their part in every battle and that every encounter rewards thoughtful planning and provides players with meaningful decisions to make. The developers are also hard at work on the progression systems in order to make developing the party more engaging: The goal is to give players more reasons to experiment with different skills and adapt their tactics to the challenges. During this longer period of waiting, fans of Shadow of the Road can look forward to more trailers and insights into the game world soon.

sources.text: Gears of War E-Day é bom? Confira review com o novo exclusivo do Xbox e PC O Xbox Game Pass é um dos serviços de assinatura de games mais democráticos da atualidade, já que é possível acessá-lo de diferentes plataformas — incluindo os próprios, consoles da Microsoft, assim como no PC, nuvem, celulares, tablets e até Smart TVs Samsung e LG com modelos de 2022 para cá. Felizmente, seu catálogo também é atualizado quase que semanalmente, trazendo inúmeras opções para os assinantes aproveitarem — e o melhor de tudo: gastando pouco em comparação às novas tendências de preços da indústria. Se veio em busca de novos jogos para jogar através do Xbox Game Pass , está no lugar certo. O serviço ganhou um reforço de peso esta semana com a chegada de quatro títulos para os assinantes aproveitarem. Confira abaixo mais informações sobre as novas aventuras! Gears of War: E-Day é uma prequel do primeiro jogo da franquia e acompanha Marcus Fenix e Dominic Santiago durante o Dia da Emergência, 14 anos antes dos acontecimentos originais. A campanha mostra o surgimento da Horda Locust e o início da batalha pela sobrevivência da humanidade. O game aposta na ação brutal característica da série, com uma história focada na origem dos personagens e do conflito contra os Locust. Gears of War: E-Day chegou no primeiro dia ao Xbox Game Pass. Echo Weaver é um metroidvania com foco em exploração, conhecimento e manipulação do tempo. No papel do último Tecelão, o jogador precisa aprender com cada ciclo temporal e utilizar as anomalias para encontrar uma forma de quebrar a repetição. A aventura combina exploração e resolução de mistérios, fazendo com que as informações obtidas durante as tentativas sejam parte essencial da progressão. O jogo também chegou no primeiro dia ao Xbox Game Pass. Forever Ago acompanha Alfred, que parte em uma viagem pelo norte após uma tragédia que muda sua vida. A aventura solo é centrada na exploração de diferentes lugares, no encontro com novos personagens e na busca por redenção. Durante a jornada, o jogador poderá registrar momentos com uma câmera, conhecer pessoas e construir novas amizades. Claro, Forever Ago também chegou ao Xbox Game Pass no primeiro dia. Por fim, Neon Abyss 2 combina plataforma e ação roguelike em um cenário cyberpunk repleto de elementos pixelados. Na pele de um personagem lançado em Nova Atenas, o jogador precisa enfrentar o Abismo e diferentes ameaças enquanto busca vingança. A experiência é construída em torno de tentativas sucessivas, com a morte fazendo parte da progressão. Cada derrota permite uma nova oportunidade de explorar o Abismo e avançar em meio aos desafios. stories.title: Magic: The Gathering Darkhold Destiny Panel – Everything Announced
stories.summary: Earlier this year at MagicCon in Las Vegas, Wizards of the Coast revealed its in-universe sets for 2027, but that only covered three of the six planned sets. The other three are Universes Beyond — the card game's crossover brand — and now we know about another one, Darkhold Destiny, the new Marvel set.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Magic: The Gathering Darkhold Destiny Panel – Everything Announced
sources.text: Wizards of the Coast just announced Magic: The Gathering Darkhold Destiny , its latest Marvel set in a New York Comic Con panel. This is the third Marvel collaboration for the card game, but where the first two were about presenting super heroes as they already exist in Marvel canon, Wizards of the Coast was able to cook up its own storyline for Darkhold Destiny. The set revolves around the likes of Doctor Strange, Thor and Ghost Rider, all trying to work against Hela and Dormammu invading the multiverse. It's a much better thematic fit for Magic: The Gathering, and the early cards have introduced new mechanics like Vengeance, which is like the Adventure mechanic introduced in Throne of Eldraine, but evil . Even though there was a lot of information in this panel, the set doesn't come out until April 8th next year, so there are still plenty of details that WotC is holding close to its chest. And, keep in mind that there are still two more Universes Beyond sets coming next year that we don't know anything about. 8:35 pm: And that's the show. Darkhold Destiny, looks like a cool set, but there's still a lot that Wizards didn't reveal. But it's a decent start! 8:33 pm: WotC announced a special promo or Doctor Doom, King of Latveria for Avengers Doomsday. you'll be able to grab it if you go see the movie at a Regal Cinemas on opening weekend "as long as supplies last". It's the face of the Dr. Doom commander deck, and it's done in the style of the MCU, so I expect it'll go fast. 8:31 pm: One more thing. There will be three Secret Lair drops inspired by Dr. Doom, just in time for the new Avengers movie. They're not revealing which cards are in the drop yet, but there is Dr. Doom art, and they told the crowd "you'll have to guess which reprint this is". I guess we'll wait. 8:26 pm: There are new Secret Lair, a countdown kit, a giant box with 30 cards. This thing is about to cost a lot of money. Most people will get it in nonfoil, but there will be a random chance that you'll get it in traditional foil, and an even more rare chance to get it in surge foil. I guess the Secret Lair booster packs didn't work, but we're at least getting to gamble on whether or not they're foil. The Secret Lair launches November 2nd. 8:22 pm: There will be two bundles, a regular bundle and an 'Arcanum' bundle. Both of these will have their own mechanically unique promo card. Hopefully that card doesn't get too expensive! There are also two scene boxes, also filled with mechanically unique cards. 8:19 pm: For the product suite, we have Booster Packs, Collector Boosters, Prerelease Pack and Draft Night (which also has a Collector Booster). There will also be four commander decks, Strange Academy (WUB), Gods of Asgard (RGW), Midnight Sons (WB) and Lords of Hel (BR). There will also be Collectors Editions for each deck that'll be completely decked out in surge foils. 8:16 pm: The basic lands take after the Adventures From the Forgotten Realms lands, with flavor text that tell the story. Unlike that D&D set, though, each Basic Land type has two variants, one before Hela and Dormammu's invasion and one after. They look awesome. 8:13 pm: One more card, Temple of Khonshu. It's a common black/white land and it enters tapped unless you control a Dimension. Dimension is some kind of new card type, and Wizards is not revealing it yet. I hope they're better than Battles. 8:10 pm: They brought Arcane back, which was a card subtype that hasn't really existed since the Kamigawa block in the 2000s. We got a black modal spell, and a red one "Rise From the Nether" that creates 3/1 creature tokens. Bring back Splice Onto Arcane. 8:08 pm: Hela's card looks awesome, it introduces a new keyword, Vengeance, which is basically just an Adventure that you cast when the card is in the graveyard. So, if Hela is your commander, you can send her to the graveyard when she dies, then put her in the command zone when you cast from the graveyard, and make a little loop. 8:05 pm: They introduced Magik as a dual faced card. WotC didn't add all the X-Men, but Magik fits the vibe of the set, and she looks awesome. She'll be able to transform into Darkchild, and you'll be able to pay 4 life to give her indestructible. So, she'll be pretty hard to kill. 8:03 pm: But even with all the art, there has to be cards. The centerpiece is The Darkhold, a legendary artifact for three mana, and you can tap it, put sin counters on it and draw a card for each sin counter. It's like an evil version of The One Ring. 8:01 pm: The set will be themed around three different types of magic. Arcane for Doctor Strange & Co, Divine for gods like Thor and Dark Magic for villains like Hela and Dormammu. But there are some heroes might be using Dark Magic. 7:57 pm: Once they got the greenlight, WotC had to invent a lot, apparently. The first two sets were about superheroes, but with Darkhold Destiny, the company was much more interested in focusing on villains. So, we've got Hela has a foil to Thor, and the Dread Dormammu as the foil to Doctor Strange. Hela x Dormammu is quite a cool team-up, I'm not going to lie. 7:53 pm: The main heroes of the set are Doctor Strange and Thor, which perfectly fit the theme of the set. And it's not Thor as the Avenger, it's Thor as a god. It sounds like the story really came together after Magic designers pitched their idea for a darker Marvel world. 7:52 pm: There will be new crossover comics, coming out via Infinity Comics. The first issue will be out in February, with another coming closer to the April release. That should introduce people to the world that Marvel and WotC have been building together. 7:50 pm: Now they're showing off some of the art, and it looks just like something out of Innistrad. Ok, well maybe not exactly Innistrad, but very similar vibes. 7:49 pm: Marvel and Wizards have been working on this set together for years. Marvel Super Heroes and Spider-Man it was focused on just getting everyone's favorite characters in the game,

stories.summary: Blumhouse Productions has partnered with YouTube star Matthew ‘MatPat’ Patrick to create a series of movies based on viral indie horror games, and Amanda the Adventurer is first on the docket.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Blumhouse Partners With MatPat to Make Amanda the Adventurer Movie, Confirms More Indie Horror Game Adaptations Are Coming | NYCC 2026
sources.text: Blumhouse Productions has partnered with YouTube star Matthew ‘MatPat’ Patrick to create a series of movies based on viral indie horror games, and Amanda the Adventurer is first on the docket. Representatives from Blumhouse and MatPat confirmed this partnership at New York Comic Con 2026, where they said the YouTuber has “a few projects in the works” with the studio. “I am proud to announce that I’m working with Blumhouse to launch some new movies. I am taking some of my all-time favorite indie games and horror channels from the interwebs and partnering with Blumhouse to bring them to the big screen,” MatPat said at the panel. The first of these is Amanda the Adventurer, a first-person, puzzle-solving indie horror game that sees the player character unravel an unsettling mystery involving a low-budget animated children’s show of the same name. MatPat announced that he and Blumhouse are currently in talks with writers and directors, saying they’re “actually moving fast” to get this project made. “It’s horror with heart. Amanda is this horrifying but tragic character. It asks the question, ‘Can you trust the media being put in front of your kids?’” he said. This is the latest YouTuber-led film project to hit the news after Sean ‘Jacksepticeye’ McLoughlin revealed he was at the helm of an animated Bloodborne movie . And earlier this year, YouTube star Mark ‘Markiplier’ Fischbach stunned moviegoers with his self-funded horror movie Iron Lung , an adaptation of an indie horror game of the same name. Indie horror games have always had a strong audience online, and it seems that major studios are finally taking notice — especially after the success of Kane Parson’s Backrooms earlier this year. The film was such a hit that other creepypasta movies were greenlit in short order, including adaptations of The Mandela Catalogue , Siren Head , and even The SCP Foundation. Given the viral nature of Amanda the Adventurer, there’s a few good guesses as to what movies MatPat and Blumhouse are cooking up next. Probably all one needs to do is look at CoryxKenshin’s YouTube channel — could a Puppet Combo movie be on the way? (Nun Massacre would be wild to see in a theater.) For more New York Comic Con news, check out our hub of everything major announced at the convention's Marvel panel, as well as a new Avatar: The Last Airbender show and our interview with Daredevil star Charlie Cox. Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

His “Game Theory” videos have been pivotal in turning the Five Nights at Freddyâs series into a worldwide phenomenon. After that game made box office bank, Hollywood is tapping Patrick himself to develop more mascot horrors into feature length hits, starting with 2022âs Amanda the Adventurer . “The idea is that Iâm taking some of my favorite indie games and horror channels from the online interwebz [sic] and I am partnering with Blumhouse to bring them to the big screen,” says Patrick in front of a banner of Raising Caneâs Chicken logos . “We are giving them the spotlight that they deserve, the megaphone they need, because theyâre incredible.” Announced at this weekâs New York Comic Con, Patrick has been enlisted by Blumhouse Productions, the prolific horror studio behind everything from The Purge to Jordan Peeleâs Get Out , for a “multi-project deal,” reports Variety . The collaboration will be kicking things off with a big screen adaptation of Amanda the Adventurer , DreadXPâs tape-centric puzzle horror about exhuming an increasingly sinister childrenâs TV program. Patrickâs decade-plus series of “Game Theory” videos elevated Five Nights at Freddyâs flash in the pan into an unkillable sensation. Divulging, speculating and likely influencing the lore of the games, the story behind evil animatronics has grown so infamously tangled that only the most screen-addled pre-teens can parse it. Investing their own time and whichever cousins will listen to them at family dinner, Five Nights at Freddyâs didnât translate into a quality film but an amazing money maker for Blumhouse in 2023. Cheese au naturale, the whole Pizza Time Theater crew are now considerably less popular among their target demographic than their blood-thirsty facsimiles . Which other games Patrick ends up boosting into the cross-media vortex is yet to be confirmed, but we know one which isnât in the running. stories.title: Konami Planning 'Second and Third Waves' of New Silent Hill Games
stories.summary: Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Konami Planning 'Second and Third Waves' of New Silent Hill Games
sources.text: Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto. Okamoto offered a foggy glimpse into the classic horror franchise's future during an interview featured in Famitsu Issue 1965 (via Game Observer ). The series ended a long, painful drought without new games with an initial wave of new releases over the last few years, and now that this first batch is out, Konami is already looking forward to what it can do next. "All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully, so we’re relieved (laughs)," he noted. "They’ve also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it." Okamoto continued: "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we’re not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves. We can’t share specific details, but we’re currently looking at a number of projects." The first wave of Konami's return to Silent Hill – which included titles like the Silent Hill 2 remake , Silent Hill f , and last month's Silent Hill: Townfall – rolled out throughout the last few years. Townfall arrived as the most recent installment when it dropped players into the shoes of protagonist Simon Ordell in a '90s Scotland just last month. It received generally favorable reviews, with IGN giving it an 8/10 . We said, "Like the intravenous needle permanently jutting out of its hero’s wrist, Silent Hill: Townfall gives this long running series a welcome shot in the arm." It's a successful run of games that Konami is happy with, but getting here wasn't easy. After Hideo Kojima's Silent Hills failed to materialize, Okamoto said he had a hard time convincing higher-ups that more games was the way to go. However, as far as he was concerned, "just one remake is not enough," adding, "as a producer, I cannot let it end only with that." "If there were only one release, wouldn’t people think that the development is going to be cancelled again, I thought," Okamoto added. While Konami's plan to launch additional waves of Silent Hill games spells a promising future for fans who have missed the franchise, we have known that the series would continue in some form. Bloober Team, the horror-centric developer responsible for the Silent Hill 2 remake, confirmed it was working on a remake of the original Silent Hill last year. Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. sources.title: Konami is already thinking about the next wave of Silent Hill games
sources.text: Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto says Konami is looking at "a number of projects" after the first wave of new Silent Hill games. Talking to Famitsu , Okamoto said Konami was already thinking about what comes after its first run of new Silent Hill games, teasing "second and third waves" of releases. "All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully, so we're relieved (laughs)," he noted. "They've also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it. "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we're not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves. We can't share specific details, but we're currently looking at a number of projects." Interesting, Okamoto also hinted that it had taken some time to convince Konami execs, stressing that "one remake is not enough". "As a producer, I cannot let it end only with that," he said. "If there were only one release, wouldn't people think that the development is going to be cancelled again, I thought." Silent Hill: Townfall is out now. We awarded it four out of five stars in Eurogamer's Silent Hill: Townfall review , writing: "Silent Hill: Townfall is, though, an often phenomenal ride; reverent to its roots, rich with ideas, and yes, properly unnerving too. And there is, I think, some pleasing symmetry in the fact the two grandaddies of the survival horror genre - Resident Evil and Silent Hill - have bookended the year with their own distinctive highs; one with a warm eye to the past, the other taking bolder, more experimental strides". Silent Hill was resuscitated with a bang in 2022 when Konami announced Silent Hill 2 Remake , Silent Hill f , Silent Hill: Townfall, Silent Hill Ascension, and movie Return to Silent Hill all at once, with Silent Hill: The Short Message shadowdropped thereafter, too. Series producer Motoi Okamoto said that the key to the franchise's revival was to "cherish" a "strong psychological horror narrative" . "As long as that remains intact, we feel that we can be more liberal and experimental with what kind of gameplay we take," Okamoto said at the time. "So I think that's very evident in how Silent Hill 2 , last year's Silent Hill f and, of course, Silent Hill: Townfall, are all very different gameplay experiences. We feel that as long as we keep the narrative core intact, there's very much room to keep the gameplay style changing." Don't forget, Bloober Team - the studio behind the Silent Hill 2 remake - is now working on a remake of the original Silent Hill , which Konami announced in June 2025.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Expect plenty more Silent Hill over the next few years, as Konami has plans for 'second and third waves' of new games in its revived horror series
sources.text: "We're currently looking at a number of projects," says producer Motoi Okamoto. Silent Hill's resurrection is one of the happier stories to emerge from the games industry in recent years. After spending roughly a decade locked in a Konami cupboard, Silent Hill has received three new entries published by Konami in as many years, all of which arrived to positive reviews and, seemingly, healthy sales. But if Silent Hill 2 Remake, Silent Hill f , and Silent Hill: Townfall still haven't satisfied your craving for allegorical horror in foggy towns, fret not, because Konami has plenty more plans for the series' ongoing revival. In an interview featured in Famitsu (via IGN ), Silent Hill producer Motoi Okamoto explained that Konami is "relieved" by both the critical and commercial reception to the aforementioned three games. "All three titles we initially announced were able to be released successfully," Okamoto said, adding that, "they've also received high praise, and we are satisfied with it." Okamoto went on to say that the games released so far only represent the "first wave" of Konami's planned games for the series, and that there's not one but two additional waves on the drawing board. "Successfully launching this 'first wave' comes with great relief, but we're not stopping here; we must think of the second and third waves," Okamoto stated. "We can't share specific details, but we're currently looking at a number of projects." It's a very different situation from where Silent Hill was only a few years ago. During the chat, Okamoto revealed that persuading Konami's executive to pursue new entries in the series has been challenging, especially after the cancellation of Hideo Kojima's Silent Hills in 2015. While Okamoto eventually got Silent Hill 2's remake greenlit, he was convinced that "just one remake is not enough". According to the producer, his reasoning was "if there were only one release, wouldn't people think that the development is going to be cancelled again?" While Konami is keeping details of its future Silent Hill projects under wraps, we do know about one of them already. After its excellent remake of Silent Hill 2, Bloober Team is turning its attention to the 1999 original . Remaking the original will represent an interesting challenge, considering how much simpler its narrative is compared to its legendary sequel, and I'm curious to see how Bloober Team will approach it. As for whether NeoBards Entertainment and Screen Burn Interactive will return to the series after their takes on Silent Hill, this is yet to be confirmed. But according to our resident Silent Hill expert Elie Gould, both developers certainly have what it takes. In their Silent Hill f review , Elie described the Japan-set action-horror as a "true return to form". As for exploring the Scottish town of St Amelia, Elie wrote that Screen Burn "absolutely understands what makes a great Silent Hill game" in their Silent Hill Townfall review .
